sources.entry: Building Effective Agents by Anthropic - Anthropic's foundational taxonomy of agent patterns — prompt chaining, routing, orchestrator-workers, and evaluator-optimizer — and when to use each.

summary.name: Building effective AI agents
summary.one_liner: An Anthropic research post that lays out a taxonomy of agentic LLM patterns (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer, and autonomous agents) and advice on when to use each.
use_cases: Choosing an architecture for an LLM-based application
Deciding whether a task needs an agent or a simple workflow
Designing tool definitions and documentation for an LLM
Building customer support agents with tool access
Planning evaluation and guardrail setups for LLM systems
summary.what_it_does: This is a written guide, not a software product. It distinguishes workflows (LLMs and tools orchestrated through predefined code paths) from agents (LLMs that dynamically direct their own tool use and process). It describes five workflow patterns (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization with sectioning and voting, orchestrator-workers, and evaluator-optimizer) with example use cases and when each fits. It covers agent behavior, such as gaining ground truth from the environment at each step and using stopping conditions. An appendix gives advice on prompt-engineering tool interfaces, with examples such as requiring absolute filepaths.
notable: Clear taxonomy separating fixed workflows from model-directed agents
Advice to start with direct LLM API calls rather than heavy frameworks
Appendix on designing agent-computer interfaces (ACI) for tools, including the absolute-filepath fix
Includes a note that much of the tooling has changed since December 2024 and points to Claude Managed Agents
caveats: Tooling described is dated (post from December 2024); the page points to newer Claude Managed Agents docs for current approach
Autonomous agents carry higher cost and compounding error risk, so extensive sandboxed testing is recommended
Frameworks are described as adding abstraction layers that can obscure prompts and make debugging harder
